units.name: BuildAndScrollIntro
units.summary: Build eight four-byte sprite records, load palette and compressed nametable, then accelerate a fixed-point scroll. The high scroll accumulator terminates the first sweep; the delay permits an input escape.

carried_reviews.name: BuildAndScrollIntro

units.name: AnimateIntroSpritesAndStream
units.summary: Wait through the installed intro callback, snapshot eight OAM positions into word accumulators, and apply eight signed velocity pairs for thirty frames. Then walk the animation source in 66-byte steps until the stop flag or input abort. units.name: InitializeRaceScene
units.summary: Preserve the incoming scene state across the setup-scene dispatch using a balanced stack byte. Reset display and select CHR mode, clear four graphics buffers and load palette and track-dependent assets. A four-entry track directory chooses initialization; ordinary racing copies road streams into cartridge RAM, while alternate states seed a fixed player position. Initialize16racers, parameter/lookup planes, raster buffers, HUD cache sentinels and callback fields, then dispatch the selected race scene. Parameter builders calculate word lookup planes in cartridge RAM through fixed arithmetic helpers: the first has a 40-entry constant prefix and ends at 230 entries, another produces four scaled parameters, and the last transforms140 source words using season and vehicle-option adjustments. Normalize and optionally shuffle16driver identities, construct their inverse rank table, and initialize positions behind the track origin at 32-unit spacing with alternating lateral lanes. Derive per-racer target parameters from the track and selected option, clamp the signed minimum, and set inactive/sentinel fields to $ff. Store player limits relative to the track length; negative wrapped differences preserve the original representation.

units.name: RaceRasterEntryAndFrameLoop
units.summary: The scene entry transfers to the race root. The raster callback acknowledges MMC3 IRQ and consumes the completed road buffer. It preserves PRG banking while selecting CHR registers $80/$81, applies scroll and nametable bits per scanline, and uses deliberate repeated reads/NOPs for timing. The scene loop builds the next road projection and visible object list, then marks the buffer ready for the next callback. Frame callbacks snapshot racer state and update driving, HUD and sound separately; these cooperative flags prevent reuse of an unfinished buffer.

units.name: SwapRoadProjectionBuffers
units.summary: Exchange the two zero-page road-buffer pointers and clear road_buffer_ready after the raster consumer finishes the displayed buffer.

units.name: ReturnFromRaceRasterDelay
units.summary: One-byte return entry used as a timing/callback tail; it performs no buffer mutation itself.

units.name: RunRaceFrameProducer
units.summary: Initialize the raster hook and frame callback, then wait while the display consumes completed buffers. Update selected HUD/player paths, project the road and draw visible objects before setting the ready flag. The return values distinguish scene exit conditions rather than implying a new PRG context.

units.name: BuildRoadProjection
units.summary: Form signed lateral displacement from the player coordinate and five times its signed delta. Scale into a 24-bit starting accumulator and derive a signed per-row step. Walk four-byte road descriptors to the first change, bounded to 51 segments, and select an interpolation program from its segment index. Negative program tokens repeat the current signed step; the bounded type directory chooses the next interpolation handler.

units.name: RoadInterpolationHandlerDirectory
units.summary: Seventeen little-endian handler entries covering the admitted road type domain after its bias/doubling. Repeated words intentionally share handlers; zero entries remain stored data, not supported jump targets.

units.name: SelectRoadInterpolationTail
units.summary: Dispatch the next road type through the same finite directory with the end row $9b. Prepared source and destination pointers and signed accumulators are required; the directory does not establish arbitrary indirect code targets.

units.name: InterpolateRoadFullPositive
units.summary: Read one unsigned profile byte per row, add it to the high part of the 24-bit base and store a two-byte raster coordinate. Advance the base by the signed row step while Y decreases by two. At the segment boundary add the full slope to that step, then extend the signed linear tail down to row $9b.

units.name: InterpolateRoadQuarterPositive
units.summary: Apply one-quarter profile displacement and one-quarter slope, then join the common signed linear tail. Shifts preserve the original truncation and carry rules.

units.name: InterpolateRoadHalfPositive
units.summary: Apply one-half profile displacement and one-half slope to each raster row before joining the signed linear tail.

units.name: InterpolateRoadThreeQuartersPositive
units.summary: Build three-quarters of the profile and slope with shifts and additions; write descending raster word pairs and join the shared tail at the boundary.

units.name: InterpolateRoadFiveQuartersPositive
units.summary: Combine the full profile/slope with a quarter component, add to the road base, and write descending raster coordinate words.

units.name: InterpolateRoadQuarterNegative
units.summary: Subtract one-quarter profile displacement and slope from the road base and signed step. Carry/borrow propagation keeps the three-byte accumulator coherent.

units.name: InterpolateRoadHalfNegative
units.summary: Subtract one-half profile displacement and slope; continue the shared signed tail after reaching the segment boundary.

units.name: InterpolateRoadThreeQuartersNegative
units.summary: Build the three-quarter profile/slope contribution with shifts and subtract it from the base and step before extending the linear tail.

units.name: InterpolateRoadFullNegative
units.summary: Subtract a full profile sample per row and a full slope at the segment boundary, retaining the 24-bit signed base and16-bit raster destination.

units.name: InterpolateRoadFiveQuartersNegative
units.summary: Subtract the full plus quarter profile and slope contribution. The row boundary and prepared pointers are shared with the other interpolation entries.

units.name: InterpolateRoadThreeHalvesNegative
units.summary: Subtract the full plus half profile and slope contribution and then finish the common signed linear tail.

units.name: InterpolateRoadDoubleNegative
units.summary: Double the profile and slope with their original field widths before subtraction. Write raster word pairs until the boundary and finish at row $9b.

units.name: DrawRacersAheadInRoadView
units.summary: Walk the ordered render snapshot backward, wrapping at the active count. Reject inactive or distant racers, normalize wrapped distance, derive perspective scale and lateral screen position, and select the sprite frame through the finite distance table. Draw at most six accepted composites, stopping early if the renderer reports OAM exhaustion.

units.name: DrawRacersBehindInRoadView
units.summary: Walk render order forward and apply the alternate distant-view scale and sprite selection. Reject out-of-range or inactive racers and stop after four composites or OAM exhaustion. Track-length adjustment preserves wrapped distance around the road loop.

units.name: DrawRoadsideDescriptorObjects
units.summary: Walk at most52 road samples in four-byte descriptors. Project each nonzero object, using its low three type bits and mirror flag to select relative sprite data and attributes. Type two uses the mutable scene object list; all objects share the composite renderer and OAM bound.

units.name: UpdateRaceFrameAndHud
units.summary: Toggle the OAM build page, clear the queue-use flag and update driving/HUD callbacks. Advance the road graphics page from player speed with carry, wrapping three pages and toggling the pattern bit. Update AI when unpaused; practice mode temporarily supplies a second racer for collision handling, then restores the one-racer domain.

units.name: IntegrateDisplayedPlayerMotion
units.summary: Advance player distance with fractional carry, request collision/snapshot work after a whole-unit step, and accumulate signed lateral motion. Combine the accumulator with four times the lateral delta to produce the displayed scroll word.

units.name: CheckRoadFeatureDistance
units.summary: Compare the player distance against five prepared feature positions; a near nonnegative difference selects a finite road-feature handler. Otherwise clear the current feature and its clipping bounds.

units.name: RoadFeatureHandlerDirectory
units.summary: Five little-endian handler words selected by the near-feature index. Duplicates share the two ordinary handlers; the last entry selects the terminal feature path.

units.name: SelectAndQueueRoadFeature
units.summary: Use the bounded feature directory for nearby road markers, normalize the selected even index and choose one of two command streams from the season bit. Copy five-byte command groups into the PPU queue while it is available, stopping at $ff. Subsequent feature processing retains local clipping and sprite selection limits.

units.name: DrawPausedRaceOverlay
units.summary: When paused cap the OAM count at 58 and draw the fixed pause composite with screen-page zero; otherwise return.

units.name: RacePauseSpriteComposite
units.summary: Count6followed by six four-byte Y/tile/attribute/X records. The pause renderer uses its explicit origin and caps OAM count before drawing.

units.name: DrawPracticeRelativeSpeedIndicator
units.summary: Only practice mode3 draws this indicator. Compare the second racer speed plus seven against the player speed and select one of two bounded composites, then render at the fixed origin.

units.name: RaceProjectionAndSpriteBacking
units.summary: Counted sprites, relative pointer planes and profile backing consumed by the bounded road/racer renderers. Some pointer words refer to mutable RAM copies; CPU addresses do not identify new physical ROM roots.

units.name: UpdatePlayerSteeringAndRoadForces
units.summary: Read the current four-byte road descriptor and combine its signed curvature with the steering accumulator. Directional input selects signed speed-indexed acceleration; release or inhibited control damps steering toward zero. Clamp steering high byte to -15..15. Compare the magnitude against speed-dependent response planes and the saved baseline; sustained excess increments a skid counter and may enter the crash path. The following motion step adds curve and steering effects into the signed lateral velocity, clamps that high byte to -40..40, and integrates position using the displayed speed.

units.name: ApplySteeringResponseLimits
units.summary: Compare signed steering magnitude with the current speed response minus its baseline and option-dependent offset. Half the excess modifies the response step. Strong sustained excess increments the 45-frame counter; sufficient speed reduces the speed fraction and sets the slip flag. The sign determines whether the correction is added or subtracted.

units.name: IntegratePlayerLateralPosition
units.summary: When lateral integration is enabled, scale the signed lateral delta by half displayed speed. Add or subtract the product across the fraction and two-byte lateral coordinate; clear the one-frame integration flag afterward.

units.name: ClampPlayerRoadBounds
units.summary: Clamp the player lateral coordinate against ordinary or feature-dependent road edges and nudge lateral velocity inward. Crossing a prepared track endpoint enters the appropriate action state and caps speed; large edge drift at speed can enter crash handling. Apply the original option and action-state guards before changing motion.

units.name: SignedSteeringIncrementPlanes
units.summary: Two sixteen-byte speed-indexed planes of positive and negative steering increments. Index is integer speed shifted right4; signed high-byte corrections and clamps are handled in code.

units.name: ReserveRaceOamRecords
units.summary: Set the selected OAM record count from A and derive its four-byte write offset. The next entry hides all unused records by writing Y=$f0 until the 64-record capacity is filled.

units.name: HideUnusedRaceOamRecords
units.summary: Hide all remaining records from the selected builder count to 64 with Y=$f0, preserving four-byte record stride.

units.name: DrawClippedRaceComposite
units.summary: Read a counted sequence of four-byte Y/tile/attribute/X records from source_pointer. X/Y supply origin and A supplies attribute XOR, including horizontal reflection. Signed X offsets are added or subtracted with the saved screen-page byte; offscreen records advance only the source. Accepted sprites advance the destination and count, stopping at 64. Return the resulting count in X. The source pointer consumes only the count prefix directly; per-record indexing and skips preserve its exact layout.

units.name: CopyOamSuffixInReverse
units.summary: Use A as the first record index in the selected OAM page. Copy each four-byte record from the suffix into descending records of the alternate page, preserving byte order inside each record.

units.name: DispatchRaceExitAndResults
units.summary: Dispatch by scene state and continuation flags. Run the frame producer, save its result while disabling sound/resetting display, then choose the next scene. Completed or aborted races normalize driver progress, preserve three-plane distances, sort16driver indices and prepare result totals. Later code renders the result screen, animates three frame choices and handles confirmation; every scene transfer ends the current execution view.

units.name: AcknowledgeResultRasterAndResetScroll

units.name: NormalizeRaceOrderForContinuation
units.summary: Advance nonplayer progress by a track-dependent increment, restore player distance from its saved target, and sort adjacent three-byte distance values until no swap occurs. Clear lateral/propulsion backing after the ordering is stable.

units.name: RaceResultsMixedDisplayAssets
units.summary: Track-specific result scalars, nametable/display backing, encoded text, counted sprites and palette material. Actual result loaders establish subroles; retain unassigned mixed boundaries as generic data.

units.name: InstallTrackProjectionResources
units.summary: Copy the bounded projection directory into cartridge RAM, then select six track-dependent scalar fields with the low two season bits. Even track parity also copies two relative-sprite resource sets into their mutable RAM destinations. Enter scene2 through the shared dispatcher; these copies preserve the original explicit lengths.

units.name: TrackProjectionLimitsAndTables
units.summary: Track-dependent scalar limits and projection/sprite backing used by the resource installer and racer renderer. The smooth numeric profiles support lookup data; exact generator and physical units remain uncertain.

units.name: PlaceDriverWithinRankWindow
units.summary: Preserve the requested driver identity on the stack. If the lower and upper rank bounds differ, make at most100 bounded random attempts to select an unmarked slot; a two-step local search handles marked candidates. Find the requested driver in the 16-entry order, mark its old slot with the high bit and swap it into the selected slot. The following initializer shuffles driver order, places constrained identities in rank windows and creates monotonic track/option-dependent result words with bounded random increments.

units.name: RaceRandomRankParameterPlanes
units.summary: Track/option-indexed low and high base planes, masks and per-rank increments. The randomized ranking initializer uses them to create ordered result words; no exact original random distribution is claimed beyond the masks and bounds.

units.name: FinalizeRaceRankingAndReturnScene
units.summary: Finalize audio state and route practice mode to its scene. Otherwise normalize player progress and sort sixteen drivers by progress, breaking ties with preserved24-bit distance. Store rank awards, mark bonus-bearing drivers and the largest bonus, choose the next result mode, then dispatch. The following display entry shows a bounded confirmation animation: two counters independently alternate a two-frame component every23frames and a five-frame component every13frames until input or timeout.

units.name: ShowPostRaceConfirmationAnimation
units.summary: Load the result confirmation display and select the vehicle palette. Render three relative-animation frames, then alternate two components on13and23frame counters until input or timeout; restore display before returning.

units.name: SynthesizeRaceEngineAndCollisionAudio
units.summary: Disable voices while paused. Otherwise enable the selected pulse/triangle/noise channels, update the engine timer from drive ratio every eighth tick and modify pulse volume with controller state. Find adjacent racers in the wrapped rank list; their relative speed and near separation modulate a second pulse voice using signed saturation and attenuation. Slip uses a four-word timer pattern. Edge/contact flags start five-frame noise envelopes. The final LDA08/STA400E/BNE is always taken and does not fall into following data.

units.name: RunPitApproachAndScrollingScene
units.summary: The first two entries update vertical scroll and toggle the nametable bit on wrap. The scene root saves the player's distance, selected option and display state, computes the approach origin and installs the pit callback. A row-streaming loop uses a 60-row ring and16-byte source stride; balanced stack bytes preserve scene/parity state while priming the display. During motion, derive approach distance relative to the wrapped track, stream rows on tile-boundary crossings, draw nearby racers and apply bounded lateral control. Stop or service input restores the saved option and dispatches the corresponding scene. Lateral edge contact reduces the signed steering rate and subtracts a speed-scaled penalty from the parameter word.

units.name: AdvancePitScrollingRows

units.name: QueuePreviousPitTileRow

Choose direction/vehicle composites and write either forward or reverse OAM according to the alternating page. Following entries project five pit actors into screen rows, update the player distance in the frame callback and draw vehicle/player/HUD composites. Counted four-byte sprites preserve source order and attributes; the reverse writer steps the destination back seven after each record.
